# Overview

This document summarizes the functions defined in [HoTTRijke/chapter4.lean](../HoTTRijke/chapter4.lean).
Each entry includes the function name, its Lean signature, and a short description.

The file imports `HoTTRijke.chapter3` and is organized into four namespaces:
`chapter4_coproducts`, `chapter4_booleans`, `chapter4_lists`, and `chapter4_integers`.

::: {.callout-note}
**A note on implicit/section-variable arguments.** The exercises `_3_c_ii` through `_3_f_iii` in
`chapter4_booleans` do not declare their own `P`/`Q` arguments. They pick them up from the
`variable (P Q : Type)` declaration in scope (`chapter4.lean:18`): Lean auto-prepends any section
variable actually used in a definition's type as an **explicit** leading argument. This is
confirmed by the source itself — e.g. `_3_d_ii` and `_3_f_i` call `LEM P ...` and `LEM Q ...`
directly, which only type-checks if `LEM` takes `P` as an explicit argument. The signatures below
include these leading arguments.

Separately, `mySum_ind` in `chapter4_coproducts` uses `A`, `B`, `C` without declaring or importing
them at all; Lean's `autoImplicit` mechanism auto-generalizes these as implicit type arguments.
:::

# Namespace `chapter4_coproducts`

| Name | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mySum.inl` | `{A B : Type} → A → mySum A B` | Left injection into the custom coproduct type. |
| `mySum.inr` | `{A B : Type} → B → mySum A B` | Right injection into the custom coproduct type. |

## Function Summary

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mySum_ind` | `{A B C : Type} → (f : A → C) → (g : B → C) → (mySum A B) → C` | Eliminator/induction principle for `mySum`, case-splitting into `f` or `g` depending on the injection. `A`, `B`, `C` are auto-bound implicits (see note above). |

# Namespace `chapter4_booleans`

## Function Summary

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `proj_rightEmpty` | `(A B : Type) → myNegType B → ((A ⊕ B) → A)` | Builds a projection from `A ⊕ B` to `A`, assuming `B` is uninhabited. |
| `proj_leftEmpty` | `(A B : Type) → myNegType A → ((A ⊕ B) → B)` | Builds a projection from `A ⊕ B` to `B`, assuming `A` is uninhabited. |
| `_3_c_ii` | `(P Q : Type) → myNegType (myNegType (((P → Q) → P) → P))` | Proves a double-negated Peirce-like principle constructively. |
| `LEM` | `(P : Type) → myNegType (myNegType (P ⊕ (myNegType P)))` | Constructive double-negated law of excluded middle for `P`. |
| `_3_d_i` | `(P : Type) → (P ⊕ myNegType P) → (myNegType (myNegType P) → P)` | Uses an excluded-middle witness to eliminate double negation of `P`. |
| `_3_d_ii` | `(P Q : Type) → myEquiv (myNegType (myNegType (Q → P))) ((Sum P (myNegType P)) → (Q → P))` | Equivalence between double-negated implication and case-based function construction. |
| `_3_e_i` | `(P : Type) → myNegType (myNegType (myNegType P)) → myNegType P` | Triple-negation elimination into single negation. |
| `_3_e_ii` | `(P Q : Type) → myNegType (myNegType (P → myNegType (myNegType Q))) → (P → myNegType (myNegType Q))` | Eliminates double negation at a function type into a direct function. |
| `_3_e_iii` | `(P Q : Type) → myNegType (myNegType (myProd (myNegType (myNegType P)) (myNegType (myNegType Q)))) → (myProd (myNegType (myNegType P)) (myNegType (myNegType Q)))` | Extracts a pair of double-negated components from a double-negated product. |
| `_3_f_i` | `(P Q : Type) → myEquiv (myNegType (myNegType (myProd P Q))) (myProd (myNegType (myNegType P)) (myNegType (myNegType Q)))` | Equivalence between double-negated product and product of double-negations. |
| `_3_f_ii` | `(P Q : Type) → myEquiv (myNegType (myNegType (Sum P Q))) (myNegType (myProd (myNegType P) (myNegType Q)))` | Equivalence between double-negated sum and negation of a pair of negations. |
| `_3_f_iii` | `(P Q : Type) → myEquiv (myNegType (myNegType (P → Q))) ((myNegType (myNegType P)) → (myNegType (myNegType Q)))` | Equivalence relating double-negated implication and a map on double-negations. |

# Namespace `chapter4_lists`

## Types

| Name | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `myList.nil` | `{A : Type} → myList A` | Empty list. |
| `myList.cons` | `{A : Type} → A → myList A → myList A` | Prepends an element to a list. |

## Function Summary

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `list_string` | `(myList Nat) → String` | Serializes a `Nat` list into a concatenated string of element values (no separators). |
| `list_length` | `{A : Type} → myList A → Nat` | Computes the length of a list. |
| `nth_list` | `{A : Type} → myList A → Nat → Option A` | Returns the element at index `i` if present, otherwise `none`. |
| `fold_list` | `{A B : Type} → (μ : A → (B → B)) → (b : B) → myList A → B` | Right fold over a list using step function `μ` and base value `b`. |
| `map_list` | `{A B : Type} → (A → B) → (myList A → myList B)` | Applies a function to every element of a list. |
| `sum_list` | `myList Nat → Nat` | Computes the sum of all `Nat` elements in a list. |
| `prod_list` | `myList Nat → Nat` | Computes the product of all `Nat` elements in a list. |
| `concat_list` | `{A : Type} → myList A → myList A → myList A` | `concat_list l l1` appends **`l1` first, then `l`** — i.e. it returns `l1 ++ l`, not `l ++ l1`. The recursion walks `l1`, and `l` (the *first* argument) only appears once `l1` is exhausted. See *Possible Issues* below. |
| `flatten_list` | `{A : Type} → myList (myList A) → myList A` | Flattens a list of lists — see *Possible Issues* for a note on sublist ordering. |
| `reverse_list` | `{A : Type} → myList A → myList A` | Reverses a list recursively using `concat_list`. |

## Defined Example Values

| Name | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `l` | `myList Nat` | Example list: `5, 4, 3, 2, 1`. |
| `l2` | `myList Nat` | Example list: `7, 9, 11`. |
| `ll` | `myList (myList Nat)` | Example nested list `[l2, l]`, i.e. `cons l2 (cons l nil)`. |

## Possible Issues

1. `concat_list`'s argument order is easy to misread: `concat_list l l1` evaluates to `l1 ++ l`
   (the first argument ends up *after* the second), not `l ++ l1`. This is confirmed by its use
   inside `reverse_list`: `concat_list (cons a nil) (reverse_list l1)` correctly computes
   `reverse_list l1 ++ [a]`, the standard recursive definition of list reversal, only because of
   this argument order.
2. Because `flatten_list` is implemented as
   `concat_list a (flatten_list ll1)` for `cons a ll1`, and `concat_list x y = y ++ x`,
   `flatten_list` actually concatenates the *later* sublists first: `flatten_list [l2, l]`
   reduces to `l ++ l2`, not `l2 ++ l`. So `flatten_list` reverses the order of the sublists
   relative to what a reader would normally expect from a "flatten" function, while preserving
   the order of elements *within* each sublist.

# Namespace `chapter4_integers`

## Function Summary

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `addNaturalToZ` | `(n : myN) → (z : myZ) → myZ` | Adds a positive natural amount to an integer by repeated `succZ`. |
| `subtractNaturalFromZ` | `(n : myN) → (z : myZ) → myZ` | Subtracts a positive natural amount from an integer by repeated `predZ`. |
| `myAddZ` | `(a b : myZ) → myZ` | Integer addition by case analysis on the second argument. |
| `multNaturalWithZ` | `(a : myZ) → (b : myN) → myZ` | Multiplies an integer by a positive natural through repeated `myAddZ`. |
| `myMultZ` | `(a b : myZ) → myZ` | Integer multiplication by reducing to `multNaturalWithZ` and applying sign handling via `negative`. |

## Instances

| Name | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Add myZ` | `instance : Add myZ` | Registers `myAddZ` for the `+` operator. |
| `Mul myZ` | `instance : Mul myZ` | Registers `myMultZ` for the `*` operator. |

# Notes

- The booleans section develops constructive logic transformations using `myNegType` and
  `myEquiv` from `chapter3.lean`, and several of its definitions rely on section-variable
  auto-binding — see the callout at the top of this document.
- The list type uses a custom inductive encoding where `cons` takes an element and then a list.
- Integer operations rely on the predecessor/successor machinery (`predZ`, `succZ`) defined in
  `chapter3.lean`.
- `chapter4_coproducts` (`mySum`, `mySum_ind`) was previously undocumented; it is now covered
  above.
